item.title: Maintain particle locality
item.description:
Group particles by a bounded grid cell when profiling shows a locality-sensitive access pattern. Start with systems and kernels and selections. This stage executes on host; device movement follows experimental device rules, and spatial classification and maintenance still run on host after copy-back. Locality optimization does not supply an exact neighbor query.

Declare eligible classifier inputs

Keep position, velocity, and time separate from placement policy.

@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time."""

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Time(Copyable, Movable):
    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32

The classifier below reads Position; movement can write it without changing the entity’s component composition. Stable entity handles survive placement changes, while component references and row indices do not.

Define a deterministic SpatialClassifier and a matching read-only accessor.

comptime spatial_filter = Filter().read[Position]().exclude[Int32]()


@fieldwise_init
struct Grid(SpatialClassifier):
    """Classifies eligible particles by a bounded planar Morton cell."""

    comptime Accessor = EntityAccessor[spatial_filter]
    var cell_size: Float64

    def classify(self, entity: Self.Accessor) raises -> UInt64:
        """Reads only the declared position input.

        Args:
            entity: Borrowed classifier inputs; never retained.

        Raises:
            Error: If the cell width, coordinates, or cell bounds are invalid.

        Returns:
            The exact cell's Morton key.
        """
        ref position = entity.get[Position]()
        return morton_key_3d(
            grid_cell(Float64(position.x), self.cell_size),
            grid_cell(Float64(position.y), self.cell_size),
        )

spatial_filter classifies entities with Position and no Int32 marker. Only matching archetypes participate. Accessor must exactly match the registration filter, all filter types must belong to the world, and writable include/write inputs are rejected. Ordinary include/exclude/exclusive membership rules still apply. The world owns one copyable classifier value; a second registration raises. Do not mutate the world or retain accessors or references from classify.

grid_cell uses floor: -0.1 at cell width 1 becomes cell -1. Coordinates and cell width must be finite, width positive, and resulting cells in [-1048576, 1048575]. morton_key_3d biases each signed 21-bit axis and interleaves its bits into a collision-free 63-bit key, with z=0 for this planar simulation. Invalid inputs raise; they never clamp or wrap. Use an application encoding if these bounds do not fit.

Run movement before explicit maintenance

The movement filter and kernel stay visible alongside their classifier.

comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]()
comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]()


def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]):
    """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length.

    Args:
        context: Matching rows and read-only time.
    """
    ref time = context.resources.get[Time]()
    for particle in context:
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
        position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta
        position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta

Movement declares Position writable, so Larecs marks eligible matching identities dirty. Read-only declarations or unrelated component writes do not invalidate classifier inputs. Values change immediately; placement waits.

Call World.maintain_spatial at the chosen boundary after execution.

@fieldwise_init
struct Move(System):
    """Moves particles and then refreshes their physical placement."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Runs explicit maintenance after movement completes.

        Args:
            context: Access to the unlocked world.

        Raises:
            Error: If execution or maintenance fails.
        """
        context.run[move]()
        context.world[].maintain_spatial()

Move.update waits for the synchronous kernel, then classifies dirty inputs using their final host values. Kernel completion and system completion do not invoke maintenance automatically. End every query/selection first, including empty or exhausted cursors. Discard component references before maintenance, even when you expect a clean no-op, and reacquire them by entity handle.

Compare row ordering with growable partitions

Registration chooses the placement policy; it does not classify or move rows. The checked driver runs the same setup under each policy.

def run_stage[partitioned: Bool]() raises:
    """Checks the same identities and values under both placement policies.

    Parameters:
        partitioned: Choose growable cluster stores instead of row ordering.

    Raises:
        Error: If classification, selection, movement, or checks fail.
    """
    var world = World[Position, Velocity, Int32]()
    world.resources.add(Time(1))
    var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0.5, 0), Velocity(1, 0))
    var climber = world.storage.add_entity(Position(1.5, 0), Velocity(0, 2))
    var excluded = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-1, 0), Int32(1))
    world.register_spatial_classifier[spatial_filter](
        Grid(cell_size=1), partitioned=partitioned
    )
    world.maintain_spatial()
    assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 0.5)
    assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](excluded).x, -1)

partitioned=False is the default: maintenance sorts eligible rows by ascending numeric key within their component-defined stores. Equal keys become contiguous; tie order is not guaranteed. partitioned=True keeps one growable dense SoA store per (logical archetype, cluster key). Capacity starts at one row and doubles as needed. There is no fixed partition row limit or separate chunk-size setting; key/cell policy controls population. Store traversal is not globally key-sorted, and separate clusters need not have adjacent allocations.

The figure contrasts the two layouts after explicit maintenance.

Scroll horizontally to read the full figure.

The same logical archetype supports two placement policies.

Letter labels are identities and colors plus key labels identify clusters. All component columns and entity IDs move together. Row ordering can move unchanged entities to restore contiguous groups. Partition mode moves a changed identity into its destination cluster and repairs a source swap-removal; growing the destination can relocate its existing rows too. Creation and component transitions stage rows until maintenance; ordinary queries and host/device kernels still visit matching staged rows. Same-composition replacement stays in its current physical store until refreshed. Maintenance releases empty cluster/staging row allocations; nonempty stores retain capacity.

Select exact maintained cluster membership

The driver captures key (0, 0) after maintenance, intersecting it with a component filter across logical archetypes.

comptime if partitioned:
    # New rows are visible to ordinary execution while still staged.
    var staged = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0.25, 0))
    assert_equal(len(world.storage.query[Filter().read[Position]()]()), 4)
    var context = SystemContext(world)
    with assert_raises():
        _ = context.select_cluster[Filter().read[Position]()](
            morton_key_3d(0, 0)
        )
    world.maintain_spatial()
    var clean_context = SystemContext(world)
    var selected = clean_context.select_cluster[Filter().read[Position]()](
        morton_key_3d(0, 0)
    )
    assert_equal(
        len(selected), 2
    )  # walker and staged; two logical archetypes
    selected.run[move]()  # only walker has Velocity
    assert_equal(len(selected), 2)  # membership stays fixed after the write
    selected^.release()
    world.maintain_spatial()
    assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 1.5)
    assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](staged).x, 0.25)

SystemContext.select_cluster requires partition mode, clean maintenance, and an unlocked world. Its selection initially contains walker and staged, even though only walker has Velocity and matches move. Movement changes walker’s cell, but the selection’s membership stays fixed until release; refresh placement before acquiring the next cluster selection. Even an empty result owns a structural lock. This is exact equality to the maintained key, not a radius query. Morton key adjacency does not guarantee spatial adjacency. Enumerate relevant cells and check actual distances, or build a separate spatial index, for exact neighbors.

Track dirty inputs and choose a cadence

A maintenance pass classifies each distinct dirty eligible identity once. Repeated writes deduplicate; a clean pass scans no rows. Registration, structural changes, and full invalidation request a full rebuild. If every allocated identity is dirty, maintenance uses contiguous full classification.

Mutable storage.get[Position] marks inputs even if you only read; use read or read-only queries for observation. Setters, declared writable host/threaded ranges, and device copy-back mark affected inputs conservatively. Raw pointers or low-level storage writes bypass tracking: call world.storage.mark_spatial_dirty(entity) for each affected live identity or World.invalidate_spatial for a full rebuild. External policy changes also need full invalidation. These calls invalidate without moving rows.

Classifier errors preserve committed keys and row order and retain dirty state for retry. All fallible classification and reorder planning precedes movement; fatal allocation/lifecycle failures offer no rollback. Fix the input or policy and retry at an unlocked boundary.

Measure maintenance together with your workload. Wide component rows increase bytes moved; sparse partitions add allocations and metadata; ordinary scans pay binding/traversal per physical store. Active maintenance still copies identity-capacity keys and rebuilds a temporary cluster directory, and cluster selection scans store metadata. Structural-heavy steps request full rebuilds. A locality-sensitive pass can benefit without improving a full step; compare both complete-step costs.

Execute and troubleshoot

The final driver checks negative flooring and bounds, both placement policies, staging, fixed selection membership, and positions retrieved by stable handle.

def main() raises:
    """Checks grid bounds, default ordering, and partitioned selections.

    Raises:
        Error: If any spatial contract check fails.
    """
    assert_equal(grid_cell(-0.1, 1), -1)
    with assert_raises():
        _ = grid_cell(1048576, 1)
    with assert_raises():
        _ = morton_key_3d(0, -1048577)
    run_stage[False]()
    run_stage[True]()
    print("PASS: row ordering, partition staging, exact selections, and bounds")

Run pixi run mojo run -I src examples/particles/spatial.mojo from the repository root. Its PASS covers host spatial execution, not device spatial validation.

Failure Recovery
Dirty cluster selection Release old selections, finish explicit maintenance, then select again.
Locked-world maintenance/selection End live queries, selections, and storage ranges, even if exhausted or empty.
Invalid grid/Morton coordinate Check finite inputs, positive width and bounds; change the application encoding if needed.
Unexpected placement after raw writes Mark affected live identities or fully invalidate, then maintain. Do not reuse escaped references after maintenance.

The spatial reference links exact declarations; the partition benchmark records scoped measurements rather than a general speed guarantee.

Complete program: examples/particles/spatial.mojo 
"""Checks explicit spatial maintenance and exact particle cluster selection."""

from std.testing import assert_almost_equal, assert_equal
from larecs import (
    ExecutionBackend,
    Filter,
    KernelContext,
    Resources,
    Scheduler,
    System,
    SystemContext,
    World,
)
from std.testing import assert_raises
from larecs import SpatialClassifier, grid_cell, morton_key_3d
from larecs.entity import EntityAccessor


@fieldwise_init
struct Position(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle coordinates, using device-compatible scalar arithmetic."""

    var x: Float32
    var y: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Velocity(Copyable, Movable, TrivialRegisterPassable):
    """Particle displacement per unit of simulated time."""

    var dx: Float32
    var dy: Float32


@fieldwise_init
struct Time(Copyable, Movable):
    """Shared simulated step length."""

    var delta: Float32




comptime move_filter = Filter().include[Position]().read[Velocity]()
comptime move_resources = Resources().read[Time]()


def move(context: KernelContext[move_filter, move_resources]):
    """Moves each row using its velocity and the shared step length.

    Args:
        context: Matching rows and read-only time.
    """
    ref time = context.resources.get[Time]()
    for particle in context:
        ref position = particle.get[Position]()
        ref velocity = particle.get[Velocity]()
        position.x += velocity.dx * time.delta
        position.y += velocity.dy * time.delta




comptime spatial_filter = Filter().read[Position]().exclude[Int32]()


@fieldwise_init
struct Grid(SpatialClassifier):
    """Classifies eligible particles by a bounded planar Morton cell."""

    comptime Accessor = EntityAccessor[spatial_filter]
    var cell_size: Float64

    def classify(self, entity: Self.Accessor) raises -> UInt64:
        """Reads only the declared position input.

        Args:
            entity: Borrowed classifier inputs; never retained.

        Raises:
            Error: If the cell width, coordinates, or cell bounds are invalid.

        Returns:
            The exact cell's Morton key.
        """
        ref position = entity.get[Position]()
        return morton_key_3d(
            grid_cell(Float64(position.x), self.cell_size),
            grid_cell(Float64(position.y), self.cell_size),
        )


@fieldwise_init
struct Move(System):
    """Moves particles and then refreshes their physical placement."""

    def update(mut self, mut context: SystemContext[...]) raises:
        """Runs explicit maintenance after movement completes.

        Args:
            context: Access to the unlocked world.

        Raises:
            Error: If execution or maintenance fails.
        """
        context.run[move]()
        context.world[].maintain_spatial()


def run_stage[partitioned: Bool]() raises:
    """Checks the same identities and values under both placement policies.

    Parameters:
        partitioned: Choose growable cluster stores instead of row ordering.

    Raises:
        Error: If classification, selection, movement, or checks fail.
    """
    var world = World[Position, Velocity, Int32]()
    world.resources.add(Time(1))
    var walker = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0.5, 0), Velocity(1, 0))
    var climber = world.storage.add_entity(Position(1.5, 0), Velocity(0, 2))
    var excluded = world.storage.add_entity(Position(-1, 0), Int32(1))
    world.register_spatial_classifier[spatial_filter](
        Grid(cell_size=1), partitioned=partitioned
    )
    world.maintain_spatial()
    assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 0.5)
    assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](excluded).x, -1)

    comptime if partitioned:
        # New rows are visible to ordinary execution while still staged.
        var staged = world.storage.add_entity(Position(0.25, 0))
        assert_equal(len(world.storage.query[Filter().read[Position]()]()), 4)
        var context = SystemContext(world)
        with assert_raises():
            _ = context.select_cluster[Filter().read[Position]()](
                morton_key_3d(0, 0)
            )
        world.maintain_spatial()
        var clean_context = SystemContext(world)
        var selected = clean_context.select_cluster[Filter().read[Position]()](
            morton_key_3d(0, 0)
        )
        assert_equal(
            len(selected), 2
        )  # walker and staged; two logical archetypes
        selected.run[move]()  # only walker has Velocity
        assert_equal(len(selected), 2)  # membership stays fixed after the write
        selected^.release()
        world.maintain_spatial()
        assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](walker).x, 1.5)
        assert_equal(world.storage.read[Position](staged).x, 0.25)

    var scheduler = Scheduler[Position, Velocity, Int32](world^)
    scheduler.add_system(Move())
    scheduler.run(steps=1)
    assert_equal(scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](climber).y, 2)
    assert_equal(
        scheduler.world.storage.read[Position](walker).x,
        Float32(2.5) if partitioned else Float32(1.5),
    )


def main() raises:
    """Checks grid bounds, default ordering, and partitioned selections.

    Raises:
        Error: If any spatial contract check fails.
    """
    assert_equal(grid_cell(-0.1, 1), -1)
    with assert_raises():
        _ = grid_cell(1048576, 1)
    with assert_raises():
        _ = morton_key_3d(0, -1048577)
    run_stage[False]()
    run_stage[True]()
    print("PASS: row ordering, partition staging, exact selections, and bounds")
